source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Send the client without monitoring when the destination is nearby and the expected trip is brief","B":"Use appropriate monitoring, transport equipment, emergency capability, and qualified accompanying personnel","C":"Leave emergency equipment on the unit because the receiving department assumes all transport risk","D":"Use an untrained escort if vital signs were stable at the moment the client left the intensive-care unit"}}
source_row.rationale: Critical-care transport guidelines call for a formal process addressing pretransport coordination, appropriate transport equipment, monitoring, qualified personnel, and documentation because transport carries inherent risk.
source_row.source_detail: Guideline abstract: transport personnel, equipment, monitoring, communication, and documentation; Crit Care Med 2004; PMID 14707589; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: American College of Critical Care Medicine/SCCM — Transport of Critically Ill Patients
source_row.stem: A critically ill client must travel to another hospital department for a procedure. Which transport plan best supports safety?
